b:
Dasa-bhukti, a good hora, an auspicious muhurtham, an auspicious yoga

In ordinary people's language: luck

Of two people with equal talent, only one can win.. Nature does not share out its victories the way Super Singer does.. It is a relay race

I am still running in this marathon

They say birth itself is the first victory. Avvai said it too … it is rare to be born human .. rarer still to be born free of a hunchback, blindness, deafness or impotence… I set that learned woman's words aside, since they fall short of today's feminism and dignity

The first victory that stands in my memory is coming first in the term exam… that is what I remember. That day I stood apart from everyone. Some eyes that had always looked at me as ordinary now looked at me strangely.. Wonder, joy, longing, envy: I didn't understand the words those eyes spoke… but that victory was my first intoxication…

From that day my life was aimed at it.. For me, wallowing in that high, defeat took the form of a great demon.. As the years went by I grew afraid he would catch me… From fear came devotion… Only if every god in the house came and sat in my exam file would my marks not fall short…. I believed this for a long time

While I was running like that, a speed bump… the demon caught me… In the scholarship exam I didn't get what I had hoped for. I wasn't satisfied with what I got… The scenes changed. In the same eyes, different feelings: concern, mockery, ridicule, scorn… and this time I was old enough to understand them… Some reached out a hand and saved the boy floundering in it… they are still my friends today

If I had got what I wanted that day, my life would have run down some other path, like water diverted by a sluice.. Whatever that path was, it would not have given birth to the one writing this today… In that sense, thank you to that defeat

Many of us climbing the stairs of success forget to thank defeat. Since then I have lost in many places… those defeats are the me of today… the me I enjoy..

Even if I brush victories off with a "sour grapes", the palm fruits that fall just as the crow lands stir up the high and make me run the marathon again.. But defeat no longer looks like a demon.. He is the owner of another victory..

I keep running..
note: The opening words are terms from Hindu astrology for favourable times. Super Singer is a Tamil TV singing contest. Avvaiyar's verse says it is rare to be born human, and rarer to be born without disability; the author sets it aside as out of step with today's values. In Sri Lanka, the Grade 5 scholarship exam is a high-stakes test taken at about ten. "Palm fruit falling as the crow lands" is a Tamil proverb for a lucky coincidence.
